title: Effectiveness of Matching and Retraining under Professional Conversion Programme
what_it_is: Effectiveness of Matching and Retraining under Professional Conversion Programme

sections.label: PCPs under Adapt and Grow
sections.summary: The scope and coverage of PCPs were expanded, with over 1,300 PMETs securing conversions in 2016, 20% more than 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: With economic restructuring and slowing local workforce growth, the risk of mismatches between jobseekers and jobs created in the labour market has increased.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: To overcome this challenge, we expanded the scope of PCPs under the Adapt and Grow initiative last year to allow for conversion to different jobs within the same sector, as well as to different jobs within the same company for sectors with high risks of redundancy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We also extended the coverage of PCPs to most sectors − with 50 PCPs at the end of 2016, compared to 22 at the start of the year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The result of these changes has been encouraging, with more than 1,300 PMETs securing conversions through PCPs in 2016, which is 20% more than in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Data on take-up by race is not available.

sections.label: Older jobseekers placement share
sections.summary: Of successful jobseekers placed last year, close to 40% were more than 50 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I suppose matches for the younger ones would be easier, but are there issues for the senior groups?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: But, on the whole, of all the successful jobseekers we were able to place last year, as I can recall, about close to 40% were more than 50 years old.

sections.label: Overall job matching success rate
sections.summary: The success rate across all programmes is about 60%, with 60% of PMETs matched successfully to jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Broadly speaking, I would say that the success rate is about 60%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This is for all programmes; we do not keep track of the success rate by individual programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We look at the number of PMETs who come to us and – I stand to be corrected – we were able to match 60% of them successfully to jobs.
